rationale: Start with a broad gradient to observe all 10 compounds and locate the elution window and critical pairs. A moderate gradient duration and temperature provide a useful baseline for refining selectivity and run time.
Change only gradient duration to test whether the crowded early cluster responds to slope. The steeper gradient also creates time headroom for later selectivity adjustments.

Test temperature selectivity against injection 1, since changing slope alone left the early cluster poorly resolved. Higher temperature should also shorten retention, leaving room for a shallower gradient if needed.
At 60 C only one pair remains below target, with substantial time headroom. Lengthening the gradient by one grid step tests whether that pair improves while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

The remaining critical pair worsened with a shallower gradient, so test a higher starting organic fraction to shift selectivity rather than simply extending the run. Retain 60 C, which substantially improved the early cluster.

Injection 5 reached the maximum CRF; now shorten the gradient one step to seek a faster fully resolved method. Keep its starting composition and temperature unchanged to isolate the effect on the two closest pairs.
Shorten the gradient another step to locate the speed limit for full resolution. Injection 6 remains the faster confirmed maximum-score method if either critical pair falls below 1.5.
Narrow the gradient window to recover the small resolution deficits at eight minutes. This intermediate slope should preserve full resolution while eluting the last peak sooner than injection 6.

Test whether a higher starting organic fraction can shorten retention while preserving the selectivity gained at 60 C. Injection 8 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method; this run probes the next composition step.

Test a modest temperature reduction at the faster eight-minute gradient to see whether it redistributes separation within the early cluster. The maximum CRF is already secured, so this explores an alternative route to a faster fully resolved method.

Use a narrower window to test a slope between injections 7 and 8, seeking the fastest fully resolved boundary. The last peak should still elute within the gradient, while the critical early pair is expected to remain close to R = 1.5.

Test the lower starting-composition neighbor of injection 8 to check whether greater early retention improves the crowded cluster. Injection 11 still has a subthreshold pair despite its rounded CRF of 1.000, so injection 8 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

The local high-temperature speed boundary is now well constrained. Test the opposite temperature extreme for a different elution order that might separate the early cluster under a fast gradient, while retaining injection 8 as the best confirmed fast method.

Return to the successful high-temperature window and test additional resolution margin while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes. This seeks a more robust maximum-score alternative to the faster but marginally resolved injection 8.

Test whether a shallower gradient repairs the single deficient pair at phi0 = 0.20 while retaining its improved separation of the neighboring pair. This could provide a fully resolved, higher-margin alternative with the last peak comfortably below 10 minutes.
Increase duration one step to bring the remaining R = 1.47 pair above threshold at phi0 = 0.20. This tests a second fully resolved composition window while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

At phi0 = 0.20, the limiting pair differs from that at phi0 = 0.15, so test whether a modest temperature reduction improves this alternative window. The aim is full resolution near six minutes without the longer gradient required at 60 C.

Refine the narrow slope interval between fully resolved injection 8 and marginal injection 11. This grid point may retain R ≥ 1.5 for every pair while shortening the last-peak time relative to injection 8.

Back off one endpoint step from injection 11 to restore full resolution with a six-minute programmed gradient. The last peak is expected near the gradient end, so this also tests how tightly the final organic fraction can be trimmed without a substantial hold-time penalty.

Reduce the endpoint one step from injection 8 to add resolution margin while retaining a short run. This should provide a compromise between its marginal R = 1.51 separation and the slower, more resolved methods.

Lengthen injection 8 by one step to establish a higher-margin version of the fastest fully resolved method. The last peak should remain comfortably below 10 minutes, preserving the maximum CRF if all pairs remain resolved.

Test an intermediate slope between injections 20 and 21 to balance resolution margin and speed while preserving maximum CRF. The endpoint remains above the observed last-peak elution composition, so all compounds should elute during the gradient.
Test the untried duration between injections 5 and 14 for a higher-margin maximum-score method that remains below 10 minutes. Injection 8 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved option.

Refine the established maximum-score region with a slope between injections 5 and 23, aiming for additional resolution margin without approaching the time penalty. Keep injection 8 as the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Use the final injection to test a modestly shallower slope than injection 6, targeting full resolution with slightly more margin and no time penalty. The maximum CRF is already achieved; injection 8 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.
